fatal_errors: The proposed polycrystalline material class does not match the equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals studied.
The 300–1000 K range omits the decisive cryogenic regime down to 9 K and much of the high-temperature regime up to 1373 K.

The hypothesis predicts a grain-boundary-dominated transition, although the target specimens are bulk single crystals and the reported mechanisms concern dislocation glide, inertia, and solute pinning.
It misses low-temperature phonon-drag-controlled inertial dulling, MSAD-dependent solid-solution strengthening, and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier behavior.

The generic prediction of increasing plastic deformation with temperature does not reconstruct the nonmonotonic CRSS response, including cryogenic strengthening and the elevated-temperature CRSS peak.
explanation: The response offers only a generic statement that dislocation dynamics can describe temperature-dependent deformation in polycrystalline metals. Its broad reference to thermally activated dislocation glide and a room-temperature baseline has limited conceptual overlap, but it does not identify the relevant Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived FCC medium-entropy single crystals, crystallographic orientation, compression protocol, CRSS measurement, strain-rate jumps, TEM, or MSAD calculations. It also introduces grain-boundary-controlled deformation that is inappropriate for the single-crystal target. The proposed tensile tests and simulations could establish generic temperature effects but cannot discriminate the target mechanisms without cryogenic CRSS measurements, strain-rate sensitivity, serrated-flow analysis, and composition-dependent MSAD or solute-pinning tests.
